description:
MEASURED 2026-08-05 while sourcing benchmark data for op-6sl.7.

Every literature and report host tested refused at CONNECT with HTTP 403: osti.gov, nrc.gov, pnnl.gov, digital.library.unt.edu, inis.iaea.org, sciencedirect.com, link.aps.org, doi.org, arxiv.org. WebFetch is blocked session-wide (403 even on Wikipedia). Only code hosting (gitlab.com, github.com) and WebSearch were reachable.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROJECT, not just for one bead: NO validation work that needs published experimental or benchmark data can be completed in this container. The workspace's whole V&V philosophy (VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md) rests on comparing against public literature and public benchmark data, and that comparison is currently unreachable. Verification against closed-form limits and upstream algebra still works fine; validation does not.

This already blocked op-6sl.7: the validation case is written and its admissibility criterion executes, but the two criteria needing measured nu are BLOCKED, and not one measured Zircaloy elastic constant could be obtained. The correct response was to deliver a gap list rather than invent numbers, but the maintainer's actual request — accurate benchmark data — is unmet.

OPTIONS FOR THE MAINTAINER:
- widen the environment's network policy for specific literature hosts (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web for how the policy is configured);
- or fetch the papers outside the container and commit the extracted data with full provenance, which is what DATA_POLICY.md's provenance rule expects anyway;
- or accept that validation happens on the maintainer's own machine and that container sessions do verification only, and say so in VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md so nobody rediscovers this.

Note kovan-literature exists precisely for PDF-to-Markdown literature work, so the second option has tooling already.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
DONE for the carbon/graphite half; the SiC half is blocked on a newly-found data gap (op-t33q). Delivered as tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs (5 tests) plus a rewritten scope note in geometry/triso_particle.rs.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE CHANGED. It was filed saying the wiring 'needs thermal-scattering data not present on this host' and depended on the download path (op-6tz.28). The data-availability half no longer holds: all 33 ENDF/B-VIII.0 LEAPR decks are embedded in njoy-outram-park-fork as of 2026-08-14, so every law regenerates offline with no download and no host-specific path. op-6tz.28 is NOT a blocker for this any more.

DESIGN FINDING -- this was never a triso_particle.rs change. That module assigns opaque material INDICES by design and its own doc says so. A thermal law binds to a Nuclide, not a material index, via Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering. So the wiring is caller-side composition; putting deck loading inside a CSG module would break the crate's data/transport boundary (outram-mc parses no ENDF). The deliverable is therefore the worked, checked composition, which is what a caller actually needs.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (release, this environment), barn per principal atom at 0.0253 eV:
  C in graphite : elastic 4.55555 + inelastic 0.48162 = 5.03717; free-gas C0 4.9382 -> bound 5.0372 (+2.01%). Reproduces the 5.0378 b recorded under op-nhoa against the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 TAPE, so the regenerate-from-deck path agrees with the tape path.
  C in SiC      : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291; free-gas 4.9382 -> bound 0.1329 (-97.31%). NOT USABLE.
  Si in SiC     : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.06367; free-gas Si28 1.9914 -> bound 0.0637 (-96.80%). NOT USABLE.

Root cause of the SiC gap (confirmed from the decks, not inferred): card 4 iel = 1 for graphite but 0 for both SiC decks, so stock LEAPR emits no coherent-elastic section; and the SiC decks' own comments say their coherent elastic came from MODIFIED LEAPR source (Zhu and Hawari's generalized coherent-elastic formulation). Not a defect in our port -- a capability gap. Filed as op-t33q and wired as a blocker on op-6tz.35.

The two SiC tests assert elastic == 0.0 ON PURPOSE, so closing op-t33q makes them fail and forces the docs to be updated rather than leaving inelastic-only SiC data silently in use.

NOT CLOSING outright is the wrong call either way, so: closing this bead as done for what it actually scoped (wire the bound-atom law into the shell material composition, which is now done and verified for every layer where the data exists), with the SiC data gap carried by op-t33q. Human review still owed; no transport-level TRISO result here.

description:
Landed 2026-08-11 by an agent that was STOPPED MID-TASK, so it never wrote tests or filed its own handoff. Found during the session-end sweep.

STATE. crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs is 317 lines implementing the Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder effective bed conductivity: new(), htr10(), deformation_factor(), radiation_ratio(), effective_conductivity(), stagnant_conductivity(). It contains NO todo!() and NO unimplemented!() — it is a real implementation, not a scaffold. It also contains ZERO #[test]. crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/mod.rs (41 lines) declares only `pub mod zbs;` so the tree is self-consistent and cargo check --workspace --all-targets passes with 0 errors.

THE PROBLEM. The whole acceptance criterion for this model was that it reproduce the verified 18-point reference table, and that check has never been run. An untested 317-line correlation is not evidence of anything — it is a plausible-looking implementation whose agreement with the reference is unknown.

THE ORACLE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS READ-ONLY. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/zbs.rs carries the 18-point Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder tabulation transcribed verbatim from the NRIC/INL Virtual Test Bed (reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/generic-pbr/pbr.i), spanning 300-2000 K and 11.940293-44.9504677 W/(m*K), with an exact-at-nodes interpolant already verified (max relative error 0.0, monotonic over 1701 samples). Do not edit that file; consume it as the oracle.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Test the analytic model against all 18 points and record the ACTUAL agreement with a stated tolerance and date, per the V&V rule. If it disagrees, report the disagreement — do NOT tune the model to match, and do NOT loosen the tolerance.
2. Add the analytic limits, which are falsifiable and cheap: zero emissivity must recover the stagnant-gas-plus-solid limit with no radiation term; the effective conductivity must lie between the series and parallel bounds of its constituents; and it must increase monotonically with temperature once radiation is active.
3. State the homogenisation assumption in the doc comment explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

NOTE the radiation contribution grows strongly with temperature and is what carries decay heat out during a loss of forced cooling. If it is wrong or absent the passive safety case looks better than it is, which is the specific way this model could quietly mislead.
title: tampines pebble_bed::zbs is 317 lines with ZERO tests — never checked against its reference table

description:
**Matrix solutions** on the hybrid backend. This is the highest-value item in
the epic — the linear solve dominates every FV timestep — and the hardest.

Existing serial code:

- `src/krylov/` — `bicgstab.rs`, `gmres.rs`, `preconditioner.rs`, `vecops.rs`
- `src/ldu_matrix/` — the OpenFOAM LDU sparse form
- `src/matrix/square_matrix.rs` — small dense

What to deliver, in rough dependency order:

1. **`vecops` on the backend** — axpy, dot, norm, scale. Cheap to port,
   immediately reusable, and a dot-product reduction is the honest first test
   of the GPU path. Note that a GPU tree reduction changes summation order, so
   results will differ from the serial path in the last bits; the parity gate
   must be a tolerance, and the tolerance must be stated.
2. **LDU sparse matrix-vector product** on the backend — the inner-loop cost of
   every Krylov iteration. Needs the host-side LDU-to-buffer serialisation
   (owner/neighbour addressing) done once per mesh, not per iteration.
3. **BiCGStab and GMRES drivers** that keep their control flow on the host and
   dispatch only the kernels. Do not try to move the whole Arnoldi loop into
   WGSL on the first pass.
4. **Preconditioners** — diagonal/Jacobi is trivially parallel and should come
   first. DIC/DILU are *sequential by construction*; they do not port directly,
   and the honest options are a block-Jacobi-over-subdomains variant (changes
   the preconditioner, so it changes the iteration count and must be
   re-validated) or keeping them CPU-only. Do not quietly substitute one for
   the other.
5. Dense `SquareMatrix` LU/back-substitution — small, so `CpuMulti` at most;
   flag it explicitly as not a GPU target unless batched over many small
   systems.

Known related work: `op-hzs.9` wants `outram-blender` to consume these sparse
solvers, and `op-ulo.5` notes the symmetric-solver (DIC-PCG / GAMG) seam is
still missing — so a CG path and GAMG are adjacent but out of scope here
unless they land first.

V&V: solve a system with a known analytic solution and a fixed-seed random SPD
system; compare CPU vs GPU residual histories, not just the final answer — a
diverging iteration count is the signal that a preconditioner was silently
changed. Record iteration counts and final residuals with the date.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Partial delivery, 2026-08-12 (active hours, +08): the LDU SpMV and its vector operations landed on the hybrid backend; items 3-5 of this bead (BiCGStab/GMRES drivers, preconditioners, dense SquareMatrix) are NOT done and this bead stays open.

Delivered in crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/ldu_matrix/parallel.rs (+ parallel/tests.rs), declared from ldu_matrix/mod.rs:
- HybridLdu: spmv/spmv_into, residual/residual_into, normalised_residual, diagonal_reciprocal(_into), auto_backend, with_matrix.
- LduTopology: the cell-gather (CRS) inversion of the face addressing.
- Free vecops: dot, axpy, norm_l1, norm_l2. Dispatch predicates spmv_backend_for / vecop_backend_for.
- One entry point per operation with ComputeBackend as a parameter; rayon behind the off-by-default 'parallel' feature; CpuMulti resolves to Serial when the feature is off. No GPU kernel: a Gpu request degrades to the best CPU path.

Strategy: cell-gather reformulation, parallel over cells, so each output is written by exactly one thread. Per-cell face lists are stored in ascending face order, which makes the product BITWISE IDENTICAL to LduMatrix::multiply on every backend and at any thread count (verified by to_bits comparison, and at 1/2/4/8 threads). Reductions use fixed 1024-element blocks combined in block order, so they are bitwise identical across backends too, though not to the flat sums in krylov::vecops.

Measured 2026-08-12, available_parallelism = 4, release, idle machine:
- SpMV crossover ~4096 cells (1.04x/1.02x over two runs); loses at 1728 (0.55x/0.65x); 2.5-3.5x from 32768 cells up. SPMV_MIN_CELLS = 4096, which SUPPORTS the crate-wide CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS placeholder of 4096 for this kernel.
- Vector ops cross over far later: dot from ~65536, axpy only from ~262144-1048576. VECOP_MIN_ELEMENTS = 262144. So 4096 is NOT a good single crate-wide number; that argues for per-kernel floors under op-yvj.4.7.
- Thread scaling on 262144 cells: 1 thr 6487 us, 2 thr 3481 us (1.86x), 4 thr 2322 us (2.79x), 8 thr 1830 us (3.54x).
- Deviation vs the flat-sum references: dot worst 2.3744e-13 raw / 7.9476e-17 relative to sum|a.b|; normalised_residual 7.6520e-15 (~34 ulp).

Verified: cargo test --lib --release 403 passed (default) / 404 passed (--features parallel), 0 failed, 9 ignored; --doc --release 62 passed both settings; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean under both feature settings, 0 warnings.

Left for follow-up: BiCGStab/GMRES drivers on the backend, preconditioners (Jacobi first; DIC/DILU are sequential by construction), dense SquareMatrix, wiring krylov/ and ldu_matrix/solvers/ onto HybridLdu (nothing consumes it yet), a 'scale' vecop, per-operation vecop floors, and a symmetric-matrix (lower==upper) fast path. No human V&V; AI-assisted draft.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Verification pass (third agent session, 2026-08-13).

Independently re-ran every measurement in src/krylov/hybrid_tests.rs. All
deterministic gates reproduce EXACTLY (iteration counts 43/75/35/65/13/20;
worst error vs dense LU 6.832e-10; blocked-vs-flat table digit-for-digit).
Timing benchmarks reproduce inside their stated bands; two bands widened by a
fresh run and one over-broad claim corrected (details in the doc comments).

END-TO-END SPEED-UP (the epic's payoff, 5th independent run, load 1.53->1.67,
available_parallelism()=4, release, --features parallel, best of 5):
  512 000 cells: Jacobi 2024.812 -> 815.677 ms = 2.48x; ILU(0) 1013.883 ->
  676.072 ms = 1.50x. Crossover ~13 000 cells. At 4 096 cells the parallel
  solve LOSES (0.67x Jacobi, 0.60x ILU(0)) -- 0.60x is below the previously
  recorded 0.67-0.81x band, so that band was widened.

NEW WORK THIS SESSION -- the reduction-order risk is now measured, not
disclaimed. Added gmres_flat (flat-reduction GMRES reference, sharing gmres.rs's
own givens()/HAPPY_TOL via pub(super) so only the summation order differs) and
reduction_order_flips_no_iteration_counts_across_a_tolerance_sweep: 3 mesh sizes
x 3 dominances x 3 RHS seeds x 4 tolerances (1e-6..1e-12) x 2 solvers = 216
solve-pairs. Iteration-count flips: ZERO, for GMRES as well as BiCGStab. GMRES
had never been compared under the two reduction orders before and is the
structurally more exposed solver (~4x the reductions per iteration; stopping
test reads a Givens recurrence, not a fresh norm). Max relative difference in
converged residual 2.220e-4, which at the tightest tolerance is an ABSOLUTE
difference of ~1.9e-16 on a residual of 8.6e-13.

ILU(0): sequential in both phases, not pretended otherwise. Triangular solves
are 29-46% of the SERIAL solve (4th run: 34.1/37.4/37.3/40.7%), capping speed-up
at 1.7-2.1x on 4 cores; measured ~1.5x sits below that cap. Factorisation is a
further ~24% of one serial solve, paid per coefficient update.

Test state: 510 lib (--features parallel) / 504 lib (default) / 116 doc both /
6 hybrid_parity both, 0 failed. Android aarch64-linux-android --all-targets
clean under both feature settings. No compiler warnings.
